question: Which location guarantees survive edits, deletion, movement and root changes, and where do text, node and range targets need distinct contracts?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest stop verdict, at queue position 7 in the plite-view group. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Plite owns the complete selection model, meaning text selection plus one built-in directional NodeSelection, with no plugin selection kinds or parallel selected-node stores (docs/vision/plite.md).
selection() returns a plain Range or null with no kind tags; ranges() and nodes() are the plural projections of the same state (docs/vision/plite.md).
Structural transforms map anchor and focus independently and keep backward, forward or collapsed direction.
editor.anchor holds one model-owned target with association, deletion policy and release, and resolves in any view of the same model and root; tx.anchor auto-releases at the transaction boundary.
NodeKey is editor-local live identity that never enters serialized data, so persisted and detached positions stay path-based.
Internal projected view selection is input-engine state and never becomes a public carrier or part of the document.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-12 lanes and its table and async-media consumer evidence as context, without replaying its inspected tests. Rechecked on the live tree the TextSelection and NodeSelection types, the public EditorStateSelectionApi read shape, the Anchor interface and its consumers (media insertUrl across an await, transfer, delete-backward, clipboard, composition), the private view-selection module and its absence from plitejs/react exports, Table's derived selection read, and the outcomes of the 2026-09-23 mixed suggestion deletion, TaskHub 45 and 46 and IME caret plans.
summary: The job is to address content statically, hold one canonical selection across edits, history, collaboration and persistence, keep a position alive across async work, and know which rendered occurrence a DOM selection sits in. Live source keeps one owner for each: Path, Point and Range; TextSelection (direction, affinity, next-insertion marks) or NodeSelection (canonical exact paths with directional ends), read publicly as a plain Range with ranges() and nodes(); editor.anchor and tx.anchor with resolve(view?) and release; and a WeakMap-private projected view selection in plitejs/react. Table derives its cell view from core selection through a version-keyed cache instead of storing one. The three later repairs (TaskHub 45 and 46, IME caret) fixed bugs inside these owners with no public API change and no second selection layer. The strongest replacements, NodeKey-offset points as in Lexical, integer positions as in ProseMirror, or folding occurrence identity into the canonical selection, each lose a current job or a hard law.

reconciliation.question: Which location guarantees survive edits, deletion, movement and root changes, and where do text, node and range targets need distinct contracts?
reconciliation.reason: Its Stop against universal locations, bounding ranges and React-owned canonical selection still holds; live source keeps the same distinct contracts and private projected targeting.

alternatives: Keeping distinct coordinates, canonical selection, anchors and private projected selection wins. Each has one owner and its own lifetime.

Replacing Path, Point and Range with NodeKey plus offset, as Lexical does, loses. NodeKey is editor-local and never serialized, so persistence, detached transaction specs and cross-editor transfer would need a second position system anyway.

Replacing tree coordinates with integer positions and a mapping, as ProseMirror does, loses the named-root and path addressing that schema, transfer and node selection depend on, for no current caller gain.
Folding occurrence and retained-fragment identity into the canonical selection loses. It puts a DOM projection into persisted, collaborative and historical selection, which the Vision forbids.

Deleting NodeSelection in favor of a representative range or a Plate block-selection store loses the exact disjoint membership that Table and block selection need, and it recreates the parallel store the Vision forbids.

Making every coordinate a live anchor, or dropping anchors for plain coordinates, loses. The first forces release ownership onto every read, and the second loses rebasing across awaits, such as media insertUrl.

Deleting one of the identical public type aliases SelectionValue and EditorSelection (both NodeSelection | TextSelection) is a fair naming cleanup with no ownership or behavior effect, so it does not earn a Pursue.
proofLimits: Source and plan review only; no test, browser, mapping-complexity or device run. Stop rejects the named replacements and does not certify mapping correctness, native caret parity or collaboration behavior. External editor comparisons (Lexical, ProseMirror) come from general knowledge of their models, not a source audit run here. core/public-state.ts and editor-runtime-view.ts carry another session's uncommitted document-admission edits that do not touch selection reads.
